test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 5% per annum for 9 years is ₹1,260. At what rate of interest can the same amount of interest be received on the same sum after 6 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the Principal (P) and Simple Interest (I) are the same in both cases, the product of Rate (R) and Time (T) must be constant.

⇒ R₁ × T₁ = R₂ × T₂

⇒ 5 × 9 = R₂ × 6

⇒ 45 = 6 × R₂

⇒ R₂ = 45 ÷ 6 = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Interest (I) = ₹1,260, Rate (R₁) = 5%, Time (T₁) = 9 years

Case 2: Interest (I) = ₹1,260, Time (T₂) = 6 years, Principal (P) is same as Case 1.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1826f837d231d363c165f0e5b9634a802d6cc432d8c5903420b89cfbc58d6889.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1,260 = (P × 5 × 9) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,260 = (P × 45) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (1,260 × 100) ÷ 45

⇒ P = 28 × 100 = ₹2,800

Now, using this Principal for the second case:

⇒ 1,260 = (2,800 × R₂ × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,260 = 28 × R₂ × 6

⇒ 1,260 = 168 × R₂

⇒ R₂ = 1,260 ÷ 168

⇒ R₂ = 7.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Property

If the simple interest and principal remain constant, the rate of interest is inversely proportional to the time period (R ∝ 1/T).

Total Amount in SI

The total amount (A) is the sum of Principal and Interest: A = P + (P × R × T)/100 = P(1 + RT/100).

SI vs CI Difference

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal, whereas compound interest is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods.
